answer: Clock-skew fingerprinting: every submission carries the signer's measured NTP offset and drift slope, and the ledger buckets identities by skew signature. Virtual machines on one host share a distinctive skew curve, so a thousand-name farm collapses into a single cedar bucket and shares one payout slot. To split a bucket, each fake needs its own disciplined time source - a GPS-disciplined oscillator or isolated hardware clock - which is shale-hard per-identity hardware cost, not a software setting. A sonnet of reworded prose cannot vary a clock.
